And thus at Cairo there is always to be found a considerable population of French, Americans, and of English. arxiv-2105-09614.title: Rate equations model for multiple magnetic mirrors in various thermodynamic scenarios
arxiv-2105-09614.creator: Tal Miller, Ilan Be’ery, Ido Barth
arxiv-2105-09614.description: Abstract Axial particle loss is one of the main challenges for fusion aimed, linear magnetic mirror plasma configurations. One way to mitigate this disadvantage and increase the confinement time is to use a multiple mirrors setup. The idea is to reduce the outgoing flux by collisions in the outer magnetic cells.

arxiv-2105-13136.title: A framework for data-driven solution and parameter estimation of PDEs using conditional generative adversarial networks
arxiv-2105-13136.creator: Teeratorn Kadeethum, Daniel O’Malley, Jan Niklas Fuhg, Youngsoo Choi, Jonghyun Lee, Hari S. Viswanathan, Nikolaos Bouklas
arxiv-2105-13136.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Teeratorn Kadeethum, Daniel O’Malley, Jan Niklas Fuhg, Youngsoo Choi, Jonghyun Lee, Hari S. Viswanathan, Nikolaos Bouklas. This work is the first to employ and adapt the image-to-image translation concept based on conditional generative adversarial networks (cGAN) towards learning a forward and an inverse solution operator of partial differential equations (PDEs). Even though the proposed framework could be applied as a surrogate model for the solution of any PDEs, here we focus on steady-state solutions of coupled hydro-mechanical processes in heterogeneous porous media.

arxiv-2108-00249.title: SyDog: A Synthetic Dog Dataset for Improved 2D Pose Estimation
arxiv-2108-00249.creator: Moira Shooter Charles Malleson Adrian Hilton University of Surrey Stag Hill, University Campus, Guildford GU2 7XH {m.shooter,charles.malleson,a.hilton}@surrey.ac.uk
arxiv-2108-00249.description: Abstract Estimating the pose of animals can facilitate the understanding of animal motion which is fundamental in disciplines such as biomechanics, neuroscience, ethology, robotics and the entertainment industry. Human pose estimation models have achieved high performance due to the huge amount of training data available.

arxiv-2111-01679.title: Large deviation principles for renewal-reward processes
arxiv-2111-01679.creator: Marco Zamparo
arxiv-2111-01679.description: Abstract We establish a sharp large deviation principle for renewal-reward processes, supposing that each renewal involves a broad-sense reward taking values in a real separable Banach space. In fact, we demonstrate a weak large deviation principle without assuming any exponential moment condition on the law of waiting times and rewards by resorting to a sharp version of Cramér’s theorem.

arxiv-2204-00549.title: Fluctuation-dissipation relations for spiking neurons
arxiv-2204-00549.creator: Benjamin Lindner
arxiv-2204-00549.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Benjamin Lindner. Spontaneous fluctuations and stimulus response are essential features of neural functioning but how they are connected is poorly understood. I derive fluctuation-dissipation relations (FDR) between the spontaneous spike and voltage correlations and the firing rate susceptibility for i) the leaky integrate-and-fire (IF) model with white noise; ii) an IF model with arbitrary voltage dependence, an adaptation current, and correlated noise. The FDRs can be used to derive correlation statistics or to infer the system’s response from observations of its spontaneous activity.

arxiv-2306-09794.title: Second Law and Liu Relations: The No-reversible-direction Axiom - Revisited
arxiv-2306-09794.creator: W. Muschik
arxiv-2306-09794.description: Abstract Abstract: A thermodynamic process is governed by balance equations in field-formulated thermodynamics. Especially the balance equation of entropy takes a prominent role: it introduces the Second Law in the form of a dissipation inequality via the non-negative entropy production.

arxiv-2403-04629.title: Explaining Bayesian Optimization by Shapley Values Facilitates Human-AI Collaboration
arxiv-2403-04629.creator: Julian Rodemann, Federico Croppi, Philipp Arens, Yusuf Sale, Julia Herbinger, Bernd Bischl, Eyke Hüllermeier, Thomas Augustin, Conor J. Walsh, Giuseppe Casalicchio
arxiv-2403-04629.description: Abstract Bayesian optimization (BO) with Gaussian processes (GP) has become an indispensable algorithm for black box optimization problems. Not without a dash of irony, BO is often considered a black box itself, lacking ways to provide reasons as to why certain parameters are proposed to be evaluated. This is particularly relevant in human-in-the-loop applications of BO, such as in robotics.

arxiv-2407-04067.title: Semantic Graphs for Syntactic Simplification:A Revisit from the Age of LLM
arxiv-2407-04067.creator: Peiran Yao, Kostyantyn Guzhva, Denilson Barbosa
arxiv-2407-04067.description: Abstract Symbolic sentence meaning representations, such as AMR (Abstract Meaning Representation) provide expressive and structured semantic graphs that act as intermediates that simplify downstream NLP tasks. However, the instruction-following capability of large language models (LLMs) offers a shortcut to effectively solve NLP tasks, questioning the utility of semantic graphs.

arxiv-2409-18507.title: uGMRT Survey of EXoplanets Around M-dwarfs (GS-EXAM): Radio observations of GJ 1151
arxiv-2409-18507.creator: Mayank Narang, Manoj Puravankara, H. K. Vedantham, C. H. Ishwara Chandra, Ayanabha De, Himanshu Tyagi, Bihan Banerjee, Prasanta K. Nayak, Arun Surya, B. Shridharan, Vinod C. Pathak, Mihir Tripathi
arxiv-2409-18507.description: Abstract Coherent radio emission with properties similar to planetary auroral signals has been reported from GJ 1151, a quiescent, slow-rotating mid-M star, by the LOFAR Two-metre (120-170 MHz) Sky Survey (LoTSS). The observed LOFAR emission is fairly bright at 0.

arxiv-2503-08787.title: Echoes of Self-Interacting Dark Matter from Binary Black Hole Mergers
arxiv-2503-08787.creator: Amitayus Banik, Jeong Han Kim, Jun Seung Pi, Yuhsin Tsai
arxiv-2503-08787.description: Abstract Dark matter (DM) environments around black holes (BHs) can influence their mergers through dynamical friction, causing gravitational wave (GW) dephasing during the inspiral phase. While this effect is well studied for collisionless dark matter (CDM), it remains unexplored for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) due to the typically low DM density in SIDM halo cores.

arxiv-2505-07223.title: Geometry of Almost-Conserved Quantities in Symplectic Maps Part I. Perturbation Theory
arxiv-2505-07223.creator: T. Zolkin, S. Nagaitsev, I. Morozov, S. Kladov
arxiv-2505-07223.description: Abstract Noether’s theorem, which connects continuous symmetries to exact conservation laws, remains one of the most fundamental principles in physics and dynamical systems. In this work, we draw a conceptual parallel between two paradigms: the emergence of exact invariants from continuous symmetries, and the appearance of approximate invariants from discrete symmetries associated with reversibility in symplectic maps.

arxiv-2507-23771.title: Consensus-Driven Active Model Selection
arxiv-2507-23771.creator: Justin Kay, Grant Van Horn, Subhransu Maji, Daniel Sheldon, Sara Beery
arxiv-2507-23771.description: Abstract The widespread availability of off-the-shelf machine learning models poses a challenge: which model, of the many available candidates, should be chosen for a given data analysis task? This question of model selection is traditionally answered by collecting and annotating a validation dataset—a costly and time-intensive process.

pmc-10547066.title: The Accuracy of Ankle Eccentric Torque Control Explains Dynamic Postural Control During the Y-Balance Test
pmc-10547066.creator: Shojiro Nozu, Kristin A. Johnson, Tsukasa Tanaka, Mika Inoue, Hirofumi Nishio, Yuji Takazawa
pmc-10547066.description: BackgroundThe Y-Balance Test (YBT), especially the posteromedial (PM) reach direction (PM-YBT), is able to identify dynamic postural control deficits in those who have ankle instability. However, there still exists a need to understand how sensorimotor function at the ankle explains the performance during the PM-YBT.

pmc-10651859.title: Aptamer-based gold nanoparticle aggregates for ultrasensitive amplification-free detection of PSMA
pmc-10651859.creator: Giulia Matteoli, Stefano Luin, Luca Bellucci, Riccardo Nifosì, Fabio Beltram, Giovanni Signore
pmc-10651859.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Early diagnosis is one of the most important factors in determining the prognosis in cancer. Sensitive detection and quantification of tumour-specific biomarkers have the potential to improve significantly our diagnostic capability. Here, we introduce a triggerable aptamer-based nanostructure based on an oligonucleotide/gold nanoparticle architecture that selectively disassembles in the presence of the biomarker of interest; its optimization is based also on in-silico determination of the aptamer nucleotides interactions with the protein of interest.

pmc-11448119.title: Using an integrated motor imagery and physical training intervention after knee injury: an interim analysis of the MOTIFS randomised controlled trial
pmc-11448119.creator: Niklas Cederström, Gustav Nilsson, Rickard Dahan, Simon Granér, Eva Ageberg
pmc-11448119.description: ObjectivesPhysical function is often a main focus of knee injury rehabilitation, but recent recommendations include increasing attention to psychological factors. We have developed the MOTor Imagery to Facilitate Sensorimotor re-learning (MOTIFS) training model which integrates dynamic motor imagery into physical rehabilitation. The objective is to report interim analysis results of an adaptive randomised controlled trial regarding the pre-defined continuation criteria.

pmc-12469540.title: NeuroDecon: A Neural Network-Based Method for Three-Dimensional Deconvolution of Fluorescent Microscopic Images
pmc-12469540.creator: Alexander Sachuk, Ekaterina Volkova, Anastasiya Rakovskaya, Vyacheslav Chukanov, Ekaterina Pchitskaya, Fei Guo
pmc-12469540.description: Fluorescence microscopy performance can be significantly enhanced with image post-processing algorithms, particularly deconvolution techniques. These methods aim to revert optical aberrations by deconvolving the image with the point spread function (PSF) of the microscope. However, analytical deconvolution algorithms are computationally demanding, time-consuming, and require precise PSF estimation and careful parameter selection for optimal results.

pmc-12472027.title: Anatomical Reasons for an Impaired Internal Jugular Flow
pmc-12472027.creator: Viviana Dincă, Paris Ionescu, Răzvan Costin Tudose, Mădălin Munteanu, Alexandra Diana Vrapciu, Mugurel Constantin Rusu, Allison B Reiss
pmc-12472027.description: The internal jugular vein (IJV) is of utmost importance during various surgical and endovascular approaches, including central access. It descends through the parapharyngeal space, carotid triangle, and sternocleidomastoid region. The anatomical variables of the IJV are mainly related to its calibre and dominance, number of venous channels (i.e., duplications and fenestrations), and compression sites.

pmc-13382132.title: Resilience and comfort with advance care planning among adult outpatients with congenital heart disease
pmc-13382132.creator: Sam L Tsai, Lyndia C Brumback, Ronald A Palmen, Joyce P Yi-Frazier, Adrienne H Kovacs, Abby R Rosenberg, Jill M Steiner
pmc-13382132.description: BackgroundAdults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) have a lifelong health condition that may diminish quality of life (QOL) and cause serious illness. Promoting resilience and advance care planning (ACP) can both improve QOL. The relationship between resilience and patients’ comfort discussing ACP is unknown.ObjectivesThis study evaluates the association between patients’ self-reported resilience and comfort discussing ACP.

pmc-13482384.title: Mediating effect of health literacy on the relationship between diabetes status and aerobic physical activity adherence among middle-aged Korean adults: a theory-based secondary analysis of the second year of the ninth Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
pmc-13482384.creator: Myoung-Lyun Heo
pmc-13482384.description: PurposeThis study applied Orem’s self-care theory to examine differences in adherence to aerobic physical activity according to diabetes status among middle-aged adults and to evaluate the mediating effect of health literacy. By distinguishing between diabetes and prediabetes, the study aimed to reflect the stepwise nature of self-care demand while conceptualizing health literacy as a self-care agent.
